text:
Jake Allen has handled 11 starts for New Jersey, and the results have drifted the wrong way. He's 6-5-0 with an .873 save percentage and has allowed 7.8 goals more than an average goalie would on his shots (36 on 28.2 expected), 9th percentile. That's a sharp turn from last season, when he was +5.4 in 37 games by our measure and Evolving-Hockey had him better still on their scale.

The high-danger chances are where it's slipping: .614 against a league .684. His last night above expected by our numbers was Oct. 24 against Los Angeles, a one-goal game. Since then, four straight starts below expected, ending with four goals on just over 50 minutes of work in St. Louis on Saturday. He's 36, a Stanley Cup winner with the 2019 Blues, and our talent range still puts his true level around league average. For a goalie at this stage, the question is whether these are the bad weeks every season has or something harder to shake. You'd want to see the high-danger saves come back first.
headline: Jake Allen's high-danger saves have gone missing
